title: Qt: Conversations and I/O Graph dialogs bridge
description:
A button is added in the Conversations dialog then one or more
selected TCP conversations can be displayed directly in a new
I/O Graph dialog.

All ordinary conversations are supported, but the aggregated
ones are only supported for IPv4 now.

Closes #19051

Yes
When currentChanged is triggered, selectionChanged should be triggered as well. I would rather avoid the complexity here, and create a single response.

(I updated the code wherever possible to take into account your feedback and I'm answering below to each question respectively.)

This doesn't behave well with a single response, maybe for example when unselecting a single element of a list won't trigger _currentChanged_. At the end, the only satisfactory solution I found is this one with two signals.
please use the same naming conventions as used with the rest. In this case this variable should be used "useExtendedSelection"

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10524/diffs?diff_id=680322971&start_sha=a1105335b6b585b1272d8d25f9bd5421e5c1985a#77ef5da4ceedf349b94477fa464af0bbda2e44cd_262_262)

No need to convert here, also you should go via the protoId instead of a name comparison to ensure avoiding any conversion issues with strings.

In general though, this whole thing could be removed here, as the extended selection is only a usecase for the TCP protocol. And therefore the selection choice could be made when the tab is created. The background here is, that TrafficTab knows as little as possible about the different conversation types. But the implementation for TrafficTab does. Therefore the selection should be moved over there.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10524/diffs?diff_id=680322971&start_sha=a1105335b6b585b1272d8d25f9bd5421e5c1985a#77ef5da4ceedf349b94477fa464af0bbda2e44cd_263_262)
Yes, I changed that.
You are counting the elements, but do nothing with the result? That just costs time
Exactly, that's dead code from my debug sequence, now removed.

So if neither is empty you return and if both are empty you return? This code makes only  sense in the case that you do not want to have a parent function handle that event. If this is the case, please state so, otherwise this is dead code.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10524/diffs?diff_id=680322971&start_sha=a1105335b6b585b1272d8d25f9bd5421e5c1985a#77ef5da4ceedf349b94477fa464af0bbda2e44cd_358_356)
Yes, I changed that.

The only difference to currentIndexChanged is, that you are always refreshing the first tab. Which is - in most cases - not the TCP tab. Again, I don't really see the need for the extra handling here.

changed this line in [version 2 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10524/diffs?diff_id=680322971&start_sha=a1105335b6b585b1272d8d25f9bd5421e5c1985a#77ef5da4ceedf349b94477fa464af0bbda2e44cd_353_356)

The issue I have here is, that you introduce an additional variable, which is not required. If the follow and graph buttons should not be available, simply set their respective variables to false. That would do the same trick, and multipleSel is not required at all.
Exactly, code updated accordingly.
Why not create the displayfilter and simply call the graph with it? This simply seems to be too much "special treatment"

We need more than just one _displayFilter_, we need some kind of information for all of the selected conversations (and so far this information could not be better than their respective identifiers). This is why I am additionally passing the _Vector_, while the _displayFilter_ is still there, and will allow the "graph disaggregation" functionality if indeed the related checkbox is enabled in the conversations dialog. In that case, the _I/O Graph dialog_ will display : _All Packets_ + _displayFilter_ + the selected conversations (themselves being of course included in _displayFilter_).

While not being absolutely necessary, the _is_sibling_dialog_ argument makes the code more readable by avoiding at least one test (who triggered the _I/O Graph dialog_ ?) by making explicit when the _I/O Graph dialog_ is launched from the standard menu, or from the conversations dialog.

changed this line in [version 7 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/10524/diffs?diff_id=1231389787&start_sha=e6138a3bce45c6cb5adb1bcae5cbc33539a36ebe#97e9e93210cf080f66354cea23b9b5ad4cbd4c7b_311_385)
I so far have only reviewed the conversation dialog and company classes. I yet have to review the io_graph_dialog.

Just my personal fyi, I really like the idea. But I don't like the sole focus on TCP and some paths choosen for implementation. But I would definitely merge the final result if those issues are addressed (and pass the final review), as I think this is a very useful feature.
Thanks for all the comments, there's room for improvement and I'll spend more time on this topic.

I restricted it voluntarily to TCP as it is a new feature suggestion and I always like some kind of feedback before going too far.

Anyway there is a real technical question if we are going to generalize this, as not all conversation types are using an identifier (TCP & UDP are, but many aren't). We could either send as many _Strings_ stored in a _Vector_ (for each display filter respectively) as parameters to the dialog, or rely on something new which knows all kinds of conversations. The former is easier but not so well designed from my point of view. The latter, we can see in the _Internal Conversations Hash Tables_ that some work is required to achieve that.
Any hint would be appreciated.

@rknall I hope I'm not bothering you with this. I sent two MR for IPv4 and Ethernet that will allow this new button to also work with them, if they are accepted I'll work on IPv6 and then can we go further with this one for the IO graph button ? In this case the major protocols would be covered and we could add the secondary protocols later. I would also like to bring your attention that working on IPv4 somewhat unlocked IPv4 aggregation which seems to be waited by some people and I would happily finish the work I started on this.
You are not bothering at all. That plan sounds great!

Hi @rknall . The MRs for adding _stream id_ on the base protocols (ETH, IPv4, IPv6) were accepted and I could reach this milestone of having the I/O Graph for these important protocols (ETH/IP/TCP/UDP). I think I answered your questions above but if it's not clear, I'll do my best to rephrase.

Only one thing to add, regarding the conversations which are identified by their _stream id_ instead of relying on the _filter expressions_, as it looks lighter/cleaner (to me) but whenever we're going to merge !13601 I will need to go back to this critical point as the conversation aggregation doesn't support _stream ids_.

Friendly ping. This looks like a neat feature. What is the status ?

Hi Ronnie, thanks for the support.
I will go back on this subject this month, it's not possible to merge this easily even after adding _stream identifiers_ everywhere. Indeed, solving #16795 introduces a new behavior and I can't just rely on streams identifiers for any of the protocols. Said otherwise, the _aggregated conversations_ don't have a stream identifier. For them, building a bridge with _display filters_ as @rknall suggested would be appropriate, but for any reason I keep believing identifiers are a better way to handle _arguments_ between different _dialogs_.
Let us know when it is ready for review again.
@sahlberg @rknall I feel like the review time can start.

I think if some some features are limited to only some but not all protocols, that is fine imho for a first version.  Additional protocols can be added later when/if people need them.

This looks good to me.  But I would like rknall to resolve the conversations from the previous review.
